join_order.build: title (year IN {2006,2007} AND (title LIKE 'One Piece%' OR title LIKE 'Dragon Ball Z%'))
join_order.notes: Title is the most selective driver (tens of rows); use offsets_only index on mc.movie_id
Precompute bool[N_company+1] from cn.country_code.bin==jp_code; O(1) lookup per mc row
Range scan ci by movie_id offsets; apply ci.role_id==rt_id_actress AND ci.note=='(voice: English version)'

join_order.build: name_ok bitset[N_name+1] from name.name LIKE '%Yo%' AND NOT '%Yu%'
join_order.notes: Single full scan of name.{off,dat} builds bitset; O(1) lookup per ci row
Per surviving pid: range lookup; for each aka row track MIN(an.name)

filters.predicate: production_year BETWEEN 2006 AND 2007 AND (title LIKE 'One Piece%' OR title LIKE 'Dragon Ball Z%')
note LIKE '%(Japan)%' AND note NOT LIKE '%(USA)%' AND (note LIKE '%(2006)%' OR note LIKE '%(2007)%')

data_structures.jp_code: int16_t scalar resolved from company_name dict
data_structures.aggregation: two std::string scalars min_aka_name, min_title (lexicographic MIN, replace if smaller)

parallelism.notes: Title driver yields only tens of t_ids; per-title work is tiny. Build name_ok bitset single-threaded (one sequential pass over name.dat). Avoid thread spawn overhead.

execution_notes: Step 1: resolve rt_id_actress (scan role_type/role.{off,dat}), resolve jp_code (scan company_name/country_code.dict.{off,dat}).
Step 2: build cn_is_jp[1..N_company] from cn.country_code.bin == jp_code.

Step 3: scan title once: for i in [0, N_title): if year[i] in {2006,2007} AND (memcmp(title prefix,'One Piece',9)==0 OR memcmp(title prefix,'Dragon Ball Z',13)==0) push t_id=i+1 and remember title slice.
Step 4: build name_ok bitset by scanning name.{off,dat} once: name_ok[i+1] = (memmem 'Yo' present) && !(memmem 'Yu' present).

Step 5: for each t_id in driver: (a) mc range [mc_off[t_id], mc_off[t_id+1]); for each mc row r: apply 4 LIKE checks via memmem AND cn_is_jp[mc.company_id[r]]; break/note if any match (movie passes mc-filter). (b) if mc-filter passes, ci range [ci_off[t_id], ci_off[t_id+1]); for each ci row r: if role_id==rt_id_actress AND ci.note slice == '(voice: English version)' (length-compare then memcmp), pid=ci.person_id[r]; if name_ok[pid]: aka range [aka_off[pid], aka_off[pid+1]); for each aka row a: candidate aka_name = aka.name slice; update min_aka_name; also update min_title with current t.title slice.
Step 6: print MIN values; treat unset as NULL.
